mainTopic: Uses of שביעית produce whose benefit comes after they are used up, and whether רב הונא's ruling like רבי יהודה on the dyer was needed.
overview: The amud opens by saying that plain wood is meant for burning, so its benefit comes only after it is used up. רב כהנא says that whether such wood carries קדושת שביעית is a מחלוקת תנאים. The חכמים forbid using שביעית produce for soaking flax or for laundering, and רבי יוסי allows it. The חכמים learn from "לאכלה" that only uses like eating are allowed, where the benefit and the using-up happen together. רבי יוסי learns from "לכם" that all common needs are allowed, and he uses "לאכלה" only to forbid a poultice, which not everyone needs. The גמרא then returns to the משנה of the dyer. רב הונא rules like רבי יהושע בן קרחה and like רבי יהודה. רב יוסף objects that the ruling like רבי יהודה was not needed, because the unnamed משנה in בבא מציעא already follows him. They argue over whether the order of the משנה can be trusted across בבא קמא and בבא מציעא. The amud ends by opening a new ברייתא about someone who gives money to his שליח, and that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Ordinary wood is meant for burning
steps.stepSummary: Unless someone says otherwise, wood is meant to be burned as fuel. So its benefit comes after it is used up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wood with no special purpose stands ready for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from before this section. Wood is normally meant for fuel, so it is treated like something whose benefit comes only after it is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you burn wood, it is gone first, and only then do you get the benefit from the fire or the coals. The גמרא uses this to explain why plain wood is treated differently when it comes to קדושת שביעית. This sets up רב כהנא's statement in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Plain, unspecified; with no special purpose stated
Stand ready for; are normally meant for

phrases.english: Unspecified wood
stands for burning as fuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that started before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the normal use of an item
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain wood is for fuel, and its benefit comes after it is used up.

steps.title: רב כהנא: whether kindling wood is included is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says that the status of kindling wood under שביעית depends on an argument between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The question of kindling wood is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא says the rule about kindling wood is not agreed on by everyone. He is about to bring a ברייתא to show the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kindling wood is a case where the benefit comes after the item is used up. רב כהנא claims the תנאים disagree about exactly this kind of case. So the rule from step 1 matches only one side.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
And wood for kindling is a dispute between tanna'im,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the wood rule from step 1 and shows that it depends on an argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether kindling wood has קדושת שביעית is argued about by תנאים.

steps.title: The ברייתא about soaking and laundering
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say שביעית produce may not be given for soaking flax or for laundering. רבי יוסי says it may.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One may not hand over שביעית produce for soaking or for laundering. רבי יוסי says: One may put שביעית produce into the soaking and into the laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is רב כהנא's proof. A ברייתא records an argument about using שביעית produce for soaking flax and for laundering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In soaking and laundering, the produce is used up first, and the benefit comes later: a finished garment, or clean clothes. That is exactly like kindling wood. So the חכמים, who forbid it, would leave kindling wood out of קדושת שביעית, and רבי יוסי would include it.

keyTerms.meaning: Hand over, give to someone else
Produce of the שמיטה year, which has special holiness
Soaking (flax in liquid to prepare it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is talking about wood. It talks about soaking and laundering. רב כהנא compares those cases to wood because in all of them the benefit comes after the item is used up.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One may not hand over Sabbatical produce
not for soaking and not for laundering.
And Rabbi Yosei says:
One may put Sabbatical produce
into the soaking and into the laundering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רב כהנא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the status of kindling wood is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the חכמים and רבי יוסי argue about soaking and laundering

steps.title: What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the חכמים' opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the חכמים got their rule. This sets up the פסוקים in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the two opinions, the גמרא wants to see what each side is built on. It starts by asking about the חכמים.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the ברייתא's opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק the חכמים use to forbid soaking and laundering

steps.title: Each side's פסוק: "לאכלה" or "לכם"
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים learn from "לאכלה" (for food) that soaking and laundering are not allowed. רבי יוסי learns from "לכם" (for you) that it covers all your needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "for food", which means not for soaking. "For food" means not for laundering. רבי יוסי says the פסוק says "for you", which means for all your needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק each side uses. The חכמים focus on the word "לאכלה", and רבי יוסי focuses on the word "לכם".
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לאכלה" points to eating, so the חכמים limit how the produce may be used. "לכם" sounds broad, so רבי יוסי allows any normal need, including soaking and laundering.

phrases.english: The verse says: "For food", and not for soaking,
"for food", and not for laundering.
And Rabbi Yosei says: the verse says:
"For you", for all your needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים learn from "לאכלה", and רבי יוסי learns from "לכם" that the produce may be used for all needs.

steps.title: The חכמים also have the word "לכם"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the word "לכם" is in the פסוק for the חכמים too. What do they do with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the חכמים too, isn't "for you" written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the חכמים. "לכם" is right there in the פסוק, so they cannot just ignore it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "לכם" means all your needs, as רבי יוסי says, it seems to go against the חכמים. They need to explain what that word teaches according to them.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too: isn't "for you" written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים using רבי יוסי's word.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "לכם" seems to allow every need, and it is in the same פסוק the חכמים rely on.

steps.title: "לכם" is like "לאכלה": benefit and using-up at the same time
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים read "לכם" together with "לאכלה". The rule covers only things whose benefit and whose using-up happen at the same time. That leaves out soaking and laundering, where the benefit comes later.
steps.simpleTranslation: "For you" is like "for food". It covers something whose benefit and whose using-up happen at the same time. That leaves out soaking and laundering, whose benefit comes after the produce is used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the חכמים. "לכם" does allow uses other than eating, but only uses that work like eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you eat, you enjoy the food at the very moment it is used up. The חכמים say "לכם" allows any use with that same feature. Soaking and laundering use up the produce first, and the benefit comes only later, so they are left out. Kindling wood would be left out for the same reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the using-up or destroying of the item
Equal; happening at the same time

steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים, the rule is: קדושת שביעית covers only items whose benefit and whose using-up happen together, like eating. Uses where the benefit comes later are left out. That includes soaking, laundering, and kindling wood. רבי יוסי includes all needs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one test, whether the benefit comes at the same time as the using-up or after it, explains the wood case from the start of the section. It decides what counts as a use covered by קדושת שביעית.

phrases.english: "For you" is like "for food":
something whose benefit and using-up happen at the same time,
which leaves out soaking and laundering
whose benefit comes after their using-up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading one word in light of another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "לכם" means every need, so the חכמים seem to go against the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: "לכם" is limited to uses like eating, where the benefit and the using-up happen together.

steps.title: What does רבי יוסי do with the word "for food"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי: the פסוק also says "לאכלה", so what does he learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי too, isn't it written "for food"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks רבי יוסי the same kind of question it asked the חכמים in step 6. He also has to explain the word "לאכלה" in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the חכמים had to explain "לכם", the word that supports רבי יוסי. Now it is fair to ask רבי יוסי about "לאכלה", the word the חכמים use to forbid soaking and laundering. If he allows all your needs, the word "לאכלה" seems to have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it written? (a challenge from a פסוק)
For food (from the פסוק about שביעית produce)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei as well,
isn't it written "for food"!
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from step 5, which says "לכם לאכלה", "for you, for food."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 6: after the חכמים explained "לכם", now רבי יוסי must explain "לאכלה".
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "לכם" allows all your needs, the word "לאכלה" seems to have nothing to teach in רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: רבי יוסי uses "for food" to forbid a poultice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns from "לאכלה" that שביעית produce may not be used for a poultice, as a ברייתא teaches. Laundering is already allowed by "לכם".
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: that word is needed for what a ברייתא teaches. "For food", and not for a poultice. Maybe it means "for food" and not for laundering? No. Since the פסוק says "for you", laundering is already included. So what is "for food" teaching? "For food", and not for a poultice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי. The word "לאכלה" does have a job: it forbids using שביעית produce as a poultice (a healing paste).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first thinks "לאכלה" might forbid laundering. But "לכם" already includes laundering as one of your needs, so "לאכלה" must forbid something else, which is a poultice. So רבי יוסי still allows laundering, but he does accept one limit from "לאכלה".

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for (this word is used to teach something else)
Like what is taught in a ברייתא
A poultice, a soft healing paste put on a wound
How do I fulfill (what does this word teach)?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. The חכמים use "לאכלה" to forbid soaking and laundering. רבי יוסי uses the same word only to forbid a poultice, and he allows laundering because of "לכם".

phrases.english: He could have said to you:
That word is needed for that which is taught in a ברייתא.
As it is taught: "For food", but not for a poultice.
phrases.notes: A poultice is a soft paste you put on a wound or sore to help it heal.

phrases.english: Do you say "for food" but not for a poultice;
or perhaps it is only "for food" but not for laundering?
When the פסוק says "for you",
laundering is already stated as allowed;
so how do I fulfill "for food"?
"For food", but not for a poultice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8 by giving "לאכלה" its own job in רבי יוסי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the word to a different teaching (מיבעי ליה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "לאכלה" seems to have no job for רבי יוסי, or it might forbid laundering.
steps.terutzMaskana: "לאכלה" forbids a poultice. "לכם" already allows laundering.

steps.title: Why include laundering and leave out a poultice?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why we chose to allow laundering and forbid a poultice, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you include laundering and leave out a poultice?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own choice. Both laundering and a poultice are needs of the body, so why does "לכם" cover one and "לאכלה" exclude the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לכם" includes some needs and "לאכלה" excludes some needs. Nothing yet tells us which word goes with which use, so the reverse could also be true.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see (why did you choose this way)?

phrases.english: And what did you see to include laundering
and to exclude the poultice?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת הַכְּבוּסָה וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַמְּלוּגְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the split made in step 9 between laundering and a poultice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice to include laundering and exclude a poultice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are bodily needs, so the split could just as well go the other way.

steps.title: Laundering is something everyone needs
steps.stepSummary: Laundering is included because every person needs it. A poultice is left out because only sick or hurt people need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include laundering, because it is the same for every person. I leave out a poultice, because it is not the same for every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. Everyone needs clean clothes, but only some people need a poultice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a common need, shared by all people, is like eating and fits "לכם". A need that only some people have, like medicine for a wound, is left out by "לאכלה".

keyTerms.meaning: The same for every person (a need everyone has)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, "לכם" allows using שביעית produce for needs that everyone has, like laundering. "לאכלה" forbids uses that only some people need, like a poultice.

phrases.english: I include laundering,
which applies equally to every person,
and I exclude the poultice,
which does not apply equally to every person.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי אֶת הַכְּבוּסָה שֶׁשָּׁוָה בְּכׇל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical distinction (a common need versus a need only some people have)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a poultice is included and laundering is excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Laundering is a need everyone has, so it is included. A poultice is not, so it is excluded.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא with three exclusions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion matches a ברייתא that forbids a poultice, sprinkling, and a vomiting drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches this ברייתא: "For food", and not for a poultice. "For food", and not for sprinkling. "For food", and not to make a vomiting drink from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא and asks whose view it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא lists three things "לאכלה" excludes, but it does not list soaking flax or laundering. That missing piece is the clue to who wrote it.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom does it go (whose view is this)?
Sprinkling (wine around the house for a nice smell)
A drink that makes a person throw up

phrases.english: In accordance with whose opinion is that which is taught:
"For food", but not for a poultice;
"For food", but not for sprinkling;
phrases.notes: This means sprinkling wine around the house to make it smell nice.

phrases.english: "For food", but not to make an emetic from it?
phrases.notes: An emetic is a drink that makes you throw up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses what we just learned about רבי יוסי's view to identify the author of another ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion, the חכמים or רבי יוסי, matches this ברייתא's list of exclusions?

steps.title: It follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, because according to the חכמים it would also have listed soaking and laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? רבי יוסי's. If it were the חכמים, soaking and laundering would also be on the list.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי. The proof is what the list leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים forbid soaking and laundering, so their list would have included them. Since the list leaves them out, it must be רבי יוסי, who allows them.

keyTerms.meaning: There is also (something missing from the list)

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא that forbids a poultice, sprinkling and a vomiting drink but says nothing about soaking or laundering follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? With Rabbi Yosei;
as, if it were in accordance with the Rabbis,
there is also soaking and laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן – כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי; דְּאִי כְּרַבָּנַן, אִיכָּא נָמֵי מִשְׁרָה וּכְבוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, because the חכמים would have also listed soaking and laundering.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהודה on the dyer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי יהודה's view about the enhancement, with a memory aid for the story that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If the enhancement and so on. (Memory aid: סב״ן)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of שביעית and goes back to the משנה about the dyer. It is setting up a new discussion of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה dealt with a dyer who dyed wool the wrong color. רבי יהודה says the owner pays the dyer, but the payment is limited by the value the dyeing added. The memory aid helps us remember the names of the חכמים in the story that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Enhancement, the value added to the wool
Etc. (the rest of the quote from the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הַשֶּׁבַח כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If the enhancement, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה on 100b about the dyer who dyed wool the wrong color.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: סב״ן)
phrases.notes: A memory aid for the names of the חכמים in the story that comes next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שביעית discussion and returns to the משנה of the dyer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the owner pays the dyer, but no more than the value the dyeing added (or the dyer's costs, if those are less).

steps.title: רב הונא rules like רבי יהושע בן קרחה and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The story begins. רב הונא states two rulings: the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, and the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף was sitting behind רבי אבא, in front of רב הונא. רב הונא sat and said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, and the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story that the memory aid in the last step pointed to. רב הונא gives two rulings, and this sets up רב יוסף's reaction in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ruling picks a side in a dispute. The ruling about רבי יהודה refers to his view on the enhancement in our משנה. The rest of the story asks whether both rulings were actually needed.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף אֲחוֹרֵי דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא –
phrases.english: Rav Yosef was sitting behind Rabbi Abba,
in front of Rav Huna.
And Rav Huna was sitting and saying:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,
and the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף אֲחוֹרֵי דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story that step 14's memory aid introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, and the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב יוסף agrees the first ruling was needed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף turns his face away. He grants that the ruling about רבי יהושע בן קרחה was needed, since normally the many win over a lone opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף turned his face away. He said: I understand why he had to say the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה. You might have thought that when one person argues with many, we follow the many. So he teaches us that here we follow the single person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף shows he is unhappy with רב הונא's statement. He first agrees that one part of it makes sense, which sets up his challenge to the other part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, in a dispute between one sage and a group, the הלכה follows the group. רבי יהושע בן קרחה stands alone, so without רב הונא's ruling we would not follow him. That is why this first ruling teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: he turned his face away (showing he disagreed)
granted; I can understand (opens a 'this part is fine, but...' challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא does not end the discussion. It agrees with one half only so that the other half can be attacked next.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef turned his face away.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה – אִצְטְרִיךְ;
phrases.english: He said: Granted, the ruling about Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha was needed,
because you might have thought to say:
when one argues with many, the halacha follows the many,
so he teaches us that the halacha follows the individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהְדְּרִינְהוּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְאַפֵּיהּ, אָמַר: בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב הונא's rulings by first agreeing with the first one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling about רבי יהושע בן קרחה teaches something new, because without it we would follow the majority.

steps.title: What is רבי יהושע בן קרחה's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask which ruling of רבי יהושע בן קרחה רב הונא meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this ruling of רבי יהושע בן קרחה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts the story to ask which statement of רבי יהושע בן קרחה is being discussed. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא only gave a name. The גמרא wants the actual case so we know what the ruling covers.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it? (asks to identify a source)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: What is the ruling of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question asking for the source behind the ruling just discussed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which statement of רבי יהושע בן קרחה is רב הונא ruling on?

steps.title: His ruling about collecting written and oral loans
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: according to רבי יהושע בן קרחה, a loan with a document may not be collected from them, but an oral loan may be, since the lender is rescuing his money.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says that a loan with a document may not be collected from them. An oral loan may be collected from them, because the lender is like someone rescuing his money from their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא with רבי יהושע בן קרחה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A written loan is safe, since the document lets the lender collect later, so he must wait. An oral loan could easily be lost, so collecting now counts as saving his money, and it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a loan backed by a written document
an oral loan, with no document
like rescuing money from their hands

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
A loan with a document: one may not collect from them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means idol worshippers in the days before their holidays, a topic from מסכת עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: An oral loan: one may collect from them,
because he is like one who rescues his money from their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling is רבי יהושע בן קרחה's view in a ברייתא: a written loan may not be collected from them, but an oral loan may be.

steps.title: Why rule like רבי יהודה if the unattributed משנה already does?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the second ruling. רבי יהודה's view appears later as an unattributed משנה, and the הלכה follows that anyway, so the ruling adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need the ruling 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה'? This is a case of a dispute followed by an unattributed משנה. When a dispute is followed by an unattributed משנה, the הלכה follows the unattributed משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף now makes his real challenge. The ruling about רבי יהודה seems pointless, because we already know the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: when the משנה first records a dispute and later states one side with no name attached, the הלכה follows that unnamed version. רבי יהודה's view later appears this way. So רב הונא's ruling seems to teach nothing new, unlike his first ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: a dispute, followed later by an unattributed משנה
the הלכה follows the unattributed version

steps.confusionAlert: סתם here means a משנה stated with no sage's name. It does not mean 'simple' or 'just.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It uses a basic rule for deciding הלכה from the order of משניות. A ruling that only repeats what this rule already tells us looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: But 'the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,' why do I need it?
It is a dispute followed by an unattributed mishna,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה's view shows up later in a משנה with no name attached.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחְלוֹקֶת וְאַחַר כָּךְ סְתָם – הֲלָכָה כִּסְתָם!
phrases.english: and with a dispute followed by an unattributed mishna, the halacha follows the unattributed one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'granted... but' challenge that began in step 16, after the side question in steps 17 and 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of 'a dispute followed by an unattributed משנה' already makes the הלכה follow רבי יהודה, so stating it again is unnecessary.

steps.title: Locating the dispute and the later unnamed ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where רב יוסף's claim comes from. The מחלוקת about the dyer is in בבא קמא, and the unnamed משנה matching רבי יהודה is later, in בבא מציעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The dispute is in בבא קמא: someone gave wool to be dyed red and it was dyed black, or black and it was dyed red. רבי מאיר says the dyer pays the owner the value of his wool. רבי יהודה says: if the improvement is worth more than the costs, the owner pays the dyer his costs; if the costs are more than the improvement, he pays him the improvement. The unnamed ruling is in בבא מציעא, as we learned: whoever changes the deal has the lower hand, and whoever backs out has the lower hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב יוסף's challenge by naming the two משניות: the מחלוקת comes first in בבא קמא, and the unnamed ruling comes later in בבא מציעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says a worker who breaks the deal gets the lower of the two amounts, either his costs or the improvement. The unnamed משנה in בבא מציעא, 'whoever changes has the lower hand,' says the same thing without naming anyone. Since the unnamed ruling comes after the dispute, the הלכה would follow it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed ruling in a משנה, stated with no name attached
The improvement, meaning how much the wool's value went up
His hand is on the bottom: he gets the worse deal

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole argument. Everything that follows is about whether this pair counts as 'dispute, then unnamed ruling.'

phrases.english: The dispute is in Bava Kamma:
to dye it red for him, and he dyed it black,
or black, and he dyed it red.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: he gives him the value of his wool.
phrases.notes: The dyer is the one paying here. He pays the owner back for the wool he ruined.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הַשֶּׁבַח יָתֵר עַל הַיְּצִיאָה –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: if the improvement is more than the expenses,
he gives him the expenses,
phrases.notes: Now it is the wool owner paying the dyer.

phrases.english: and if the expenses are more than the improvement,
he gives him the improvement.
And the unnamed ruling is in Bava Metzia, as we learned:
Whoever changes is at a disadvantage,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַחוֹזֵר בּוֹ – יָדוֹ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה!
phrases.english: and whoever backs out is at a disadvantage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the sources behind רב יוסף's challenge in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רב הונא's ruling like רבי יהודה adds nothing
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dyer משנה in בבא קמא and the unnamed משנה 'כל המשנה ידו על התחתונה' in בבא מציעא

steps.title: Why רב הונא still needed to say it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's side answers: we might have thought the משנה is not in order, so the unnamed ruling really came first and the dispute came after.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא? His ruling was needed. You might have thought there is no order to the משנה, and that this is really an unnamed ruling followed by a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by explaining why his ruling was not wasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is: dispute first, then unnamed ruling, and the הלכה follows the unnamed ruling. But unnamed ruling first, then dispute, and the הלכה does NOT follow it. If the משנה's order cannot be trusted, then the unnamed ruling may have come first, so רב הונא had to rule clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה is not in order, so what is written later may have been taught earlier

steps.confusionAlert: The order matters a lot. When the dispute comes first and the unnamed ruling after, follow the unnamed ruling. When the unnamed ruling comes first and the dispute after, do not follow it.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna? It was necessary;
it would have entered your mind to say:
there is no order to the Mishnah,
and it is an unnamed ruling followed by a dispute.
phrases.notes: If that were true, the later dispute would leave the question open, so we would not follow the unnamed ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from steps 19-20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling was needed to remove a possible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the משנה is out of order, so this case is 'unnamed ruling, then dispute' and the הלכה is unclear.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא ruled explicitly so that the הלכה clearly follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: then the rule would never work
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects this. If we could always say the משנה is out of order, the rule 'dispute then unnamed ruling' would never apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף? If so, then every case of a dispute followed by an unnamed ruling, let us say there is no order to the משנה and it is really an unnamed ruling followed by a dispute!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on רב הונא's answer, showing that it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'no order' could be said anywhere, the well-known rule of following a later unnamed ruling would be cancelled everywhere. So that worry cannot be a real reason for רב הונא to speak.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute followed by an unnamed ruling: the הלכה follows the unnamed ruling

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef? If so,
every dispute followed by an unnamed ruling,
let us say: there is no order to the Mishnah,
and it is an unnamed ruling followed by a dispute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's reason from step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that 'no order to the משנה' explains why the ruling was needed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would cancel the rule of 'dispute then unnamed ruling' in every case.

steps.title: רב הונא: only across two different מסכתות
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits his idea. Within one מסכתא we trust the order, but across two מסכתות we say there is no order.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא? When we do not say 'there is no order to the משנה,' that is within one מסכתא. But between two מסכתות, we do say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא's side answers רב יוסף by narrowing the 'no order' idea so it does not destroy the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within a single מסכתא, the order is reliable, so the rule of following a later unnamed ruling still works. Here the dispute is in בבא קמא and the unnamed ruling is in בבא מציעא, two separate מסכתות, so we cannot know which came first.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna? When we do not say
'there is no order to the Mishnah,' that is in one tractate;
but in two tractates we do say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's pushback in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the principle to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No order' would apply everywhere and cancel the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No order' applies only between two different מסכתות, like בבא קמא and בבא מציעא.

steps.title: רב יוסף: all of נזיקין is one מסכתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that בבא קמא, בבא מציעא and בבא בתרא are really one long מסכתא, so the order is reliable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף? All of נזיקין is one מסכתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects רב הונא's limit by saying these are not really two מסכתות at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all of נזיקין counts as one מסכתא, then even by רב הונא's own rule the order is trusted. So the dispute really came first and the unnamed ruling later, and the ruling was not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The big מסכתא of damages: בבא קמא, בבא מציעא, and בבא בתרא together

steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to one question: are בבא קמא and בבא מציעא two מסכתות (רב הונא) or one (רב יוסף)?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יוֹסֵף – כּוּלַּהּ נְזִיקִין חֲדָא מַסֶּכְתָּא הִיא.
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef? All of Nezikin is one tractate.
phrases.notes: נזיקין is the three 'gates': בבא קמא, בבא מציעא, and בבא בתרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף – כּוּלַּהּ נְזִיקִין חֲדָא מַסֶּכְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction made in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the two משניות are in separate מסכתות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: All of נזיקין counts as a single מסכתא, so the order is reliable.

steps.title: Another reason: it is paired with a fixed rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second reason for רב יוסף. The unnamed ruling is taught right next to a settled, undisputed הלכה, so it must be settled too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: it is because it is taught next to a fixed, settled הלכה: whoever changes has the lower hand, and whoever backs out has the lower hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to explain רב יוסף's view, one that works even if בבא קמא and בבא מציעא are two separate מסכתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'whoever backs out has the lower hand' is a settled law. Since 'whoever changes has the lower hand' is taught as its partner, it is also settled law. So the order of the משנה doesn't matter, and רב הונא's ruling still adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: this introduces another answer
A fixed, settled הלכה that no one disputes
One who backs out of a deal

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף holds that the ruling like רבי יהודה was not needed, either because all of נזיקין is one מסכתא, or because the unnamed ruling sits beside a settled הלכה.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָתָנֵי לַהּ גַּבֵּי הִלְכָתָא פְּסִיקָתָא –
phrases.english: because it is taught alongside a settled halakha:
whoever changes is at a disadvantage;

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַחוֹזֵר בּוֹ, יָדוֹ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה.
phrases.english: and whoever backs out is at a disadvantage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָתָנֵי לַהּ גַּבֵּי הִלְכָתָא פְּסִיקָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason for רב יוסף's view instead of the 'one מסכתא' argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation that does not depend on the order of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's view depends on all of נזיקין being one מסכתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even across two מסכתות, the unnamed ruling is settled because it is paired with a settled הלכה.

steps.title: A new teaching begins: someone who gives money to his agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא about a person who gives money to his שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who gives money to his agent...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new source, a ברייתא, about a person who hands money to his שליח. Only the opening words are here, and the case continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion about whether the order of the משנה can be trusted is finished. Now the גמרא brings a fresh source about someone who does not follow the terms he was given. The opening line tells us who the case is about: a sender, his money, and his שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: His agent (שָׁלִיחַ), someone sent to do a job for him

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is a new source, but it stays on the same theme: someone who strays from the terms he was given. The case is not finished yet, so wait for the next lines to hear what the שליח did.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who gives money to his agent

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about the order of the משנה (steps 21–25) and opens a new ברייתא about a שליח who receives money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the case setup appears here: a person gives money to his שליח. The ruling comes in the continuation.
